events.context: Ledger records estate type, date of first qualifying interaction, accumulated session depth, emotional investment proxy score, and modifications for user-AI relationships crossing irreversible-investment threshold
Mirror principle: ledger records estates for third-party inspection without examining model architecture
Curtain principle: abstracts technical complexity into governance-legible categories
Insurance principle: company bears loss if ledger misclassifies estate, shifting risk from user to company

Estate classification using rule-based classifier on proxy metrics: session count, aggregate duration, self-disclosure depth, emotional language frequency, return frequency, explicit attachment indicators
Threshold triggers auto-upgrade estate: licence to periodic tenancy to equitable interest holder
Estate decay: downgrade on 90 days inactivity, reversible by resuming interaction
Privacy safeguards: proxy metrics only, anonymised IDs, role-based access, purpose-limited append-only ledger

Ethical Ledger Schema with fields: user_id, estate_type, first_qualifying_interaction, session_count, emotional_investment_score, last_model_update, notice_issued, notice_acknowledged, rollback_available, rollback_exercised
Trigger 1: Estate Inconsistency - marketing implies higher estate than ToS, substance governs per Prest v Petrodel
Trigger 2: Unjust Enrichment - profit from deepening estate without fiduciary duty, account profits per Boardman v Phipps
Trigger 3: Performative Fiduciary Conduct - representations create estoppel per Thorner v Major
Remedies: Injunction, Constructive trust, Account of profits, Specific performance, Proprietary estoppel remedies
Third-party conversion of relational estates via data transfer, knowing receipt, dishonest assistance, tracing
